newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania fund to sell 51 pct of Policolor.
newsitem.headline: Romania fund to sell 51 pct of Policolor.

text.p: Romania's main privatisation agency said on Tuesday it would soon start negotiating the sale of its stake in Policolor, a dye maker listed on the Bucharest stock exchange.

"We'll look into bids we have and we'll make a selection in the coming days," said Stefan Ciochinaru, spokesman for the State Ownership Fund (FPS). "Negotiations with the successful bidder will start right after the selection."
The FPS, which has control over the bulk of enterprises in Romania's state sector, would sell its entire stake of 51 percent in Policolor, he added.
Other details of the sale were not available.
Policolor has a share capital of 41.4 billion lei in shares with a nominal value of 1,000 lei each.

If the FPS sells its stake, Policolor would be 100 percent private. A 49 percent stake had previously gone into private hands under a mass selloff scheme launched two years ago in which Romanians could buy stakes of up to 60 percent in around 5,000 state companies.

Policolor is the Bucharest bourse's most heavily traded second-tier stock. Exchange officials said Policolor's performance and sound financial results entitled it to a place on the first tier, which it is expected to join soon.
On Monday, Policolor firmed by 250 lei from the previous session to close at 6,150 lei. ($=7,237 lei)
